skipper.text: Pontcysyllte Aqueduct: 1805, Thomas Telford. Eighteen arches, 38 metres above the Dee.
The boat goes at walking pace. The river's a long way down, so I just look at the tea.

unesco_walker.text: It's a World Heritage Site, you know. UNESCO, 2009.
The trough is iron, held up by stone pillars. Brave of a canal, really.

lock_keeper.text: The canal's only about a metre and a half deep. Takes the fear out of it.
Water comes in at Horseshoe Falls, up river. A weir built by Telford. It's shaped like a horseshoe, naturally.

tea_lady.text: Cuppa? We do tea, cake, and a view of a very tall bridge for water.
Bara brith's on the house. Well, on the table. You'd still pay.

welsh_lad.text: Mae'n bwrw glaw. That's 'it's raining'. You'll need it.
Also 'diolch' is thanks. Say it to the narrowboat people. They like it.

farmer_dai.text: My sheep think the aqueduct's rude. Won't cross it.
